name: John S. Lane
milestones: Granted a land warrant in 1851 for service in the Missouri Volunteers, probably in Indian or Mormon conflicts.
sources: Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
notes: Father of Cynthia Lane. His 1851 land warrant in Chariton County, Missouri, included the parcel later patented by George Francis Adams (#1).
Listed in Index of Names under LANE, page 3, no dates [Bill Allen, Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, line 5878]
Unconfirmed: Sketchy records suggest he served in the Mormon Conflict of 1838 and the Mexican/American War of 1839-1840. [Family research emails, email 12]

Unconfirmed: A land warrant or patent for John S. Lane, signed by President Fillmore or President Buchanan, was found on a CD from Bill Allen; the writer says it confirms the family's Missouri connection. [Family research emails, email 01]

Open question: Why did the Adams family move from Virginia to Ohio about 1835, and why did GFA #1 continue on to Missouri? Bill speculates about the Hamiltons going first, cheap land, a military expedition, meeting John S. Lane, or a split over slavery [Family research emails, email 12]

Open question: Which George F. Adams do the army enlistment record and land patent belong to? And which land document did Fillmore sign and which did Buchanan (George F. Adams or John S. Lane)? [Family research emails, email 01]
